businessModel: Freemium: capped free AI usage, Dia Pro subscription; owned by Atlassian since Oct 2025
paidNote: Dia Pro $20/mo (launched Aug 2025; unlimited chat and skills, personalized memory). Business tier teased, no price.
updateCadence: Frequent feature releases (about 1.x every 1-3 weeks in 2026); tracks Chromium
summary: Chromium browser from the makers of Arc, now Atlassian-owned. AI chat with your tabs, Skills and memory; Mac-only on Apple Silicon, with a capped free tier and a $20/mo Pro plan.
bestFor: Mac users who want AI chat over their open tabs
Chrome users who want to keep their extensions
notFor: People who want a privacy-first browser

pros.title: AI built into the address bar
pros.detail: Chat with tabs, summarize and run Skills without opening a separate sidebar.

pros.title: Chrome extensions work
pros.detail: Chromium base means Chrome Web Store extensions install (MV3 only).

pros.title: Active release cadence
pros.detail: v1.33.0 shipped May 28, 2026 after dozens of 1.x releases in a year.

pros.title: Free tier available
pros.detail: Basic AI features are free with usage caps; Pro lifts limits for $20/mo.

pros.title: Backed by Atlassian
pros.detail: Acquired for a reported $610M, completed Oct 21, 2025; deeper Confluence/Jira ties.

cons.title: Mac only
cons.detail: Requires macOS 14+ on Apple Silicon; Windows is still a waitlist with no date, no mobile app.

cons.title: Cloud AI by default
cons.detail: Tab content goes to model providers; memory is a Pro feature with unclear data handling.

cons.title: Limited agent depth
cons.detail: Skills and chat dominate; fewer autonomous multi-step agents than Comet or Opera Neon.

cons.title: Parent company churn
cons.detail: Arc is being sunset in favor of Dia, so priorities shift with Atlassian strategy.

signatureFeatures: AI chat in the address bar

faq.a: Yes with usage caps; Dia Pro at $20/mo removes limits and adds memory.
Not publicly. As of mid-2026 Windows is waitlist-only with no release date.
Yes, as a Chromium browser; Manifest V2 extensions are being phased out in favor of MV3.

timeline.event: Atlassian completes acquisition of The Browser Company
v1.16.0 announces move from Manifest V2 to V3

switching.note: Imports from Chrome and other major browsers (details unverified).

jsSpeed: Blink/V8 engine, Chrome-class JS speed; no vendor benchmark
pageLoad: Chromium rendering; AI sidebar adds overhead
networkSpeed: Chromium network stack with HTTP/3 and preloading
startup: Native-feeling Mac app; v1.24 focused on speed
memory: Chromium multi-process plus AI layer; RAM-heavy
cpu: Chromium-class; agent tasks add background load
lowEnd: Needs modern hardware; AI features add load
installSize: Full Chromium bundle, a few hundred MB
privacyDefaults: AI features send page context to cloud; little blocking by default
blocking: Only MV3 blockers such as uBO Lite are available
securityHardening: Chromium sandbox and site isolation; agent injection risk
patchSpeed: Chromium version not published; lag unverified
telemetry: Vendor telemetry; prompts processed in cloud
behaviourCustom: Few shortcut or per-site options documented
tabManagement: Tab groups, Live Groups, tab switcher redesign (v1.33)
searchFreedom: Default search changeable; AI prompt flow is the focus
translation: AI-driven page translation; no dedicated engine
extras: AI agent and memory; no VPN or wallet
extensions: Chrome Web Store but MV3 only since the Aug 2026 MV2 purge
sync: Account sync of tabs/settings/memory since v1.26
accessibility: Chromium accessibility stack, unverified for AI layer
longevity: Atlassian-backed, frequent releases; Arc churn noted
ai: Tab chat, Skills, memory; agent actions limited
beginnerFriendly: Familiar Chrome-like layout, AI in address bar

featureNotes.adBlocker: Only MV3 blockers such as uBO Lite
featureNotes.tabGroups: Tab groups, auto emojis, groups for meetings
featureNotes.mv2Support: MV2 removed upstream; Chrome Web Store dropped MV2 Aug 31, 2026
featureNotes.syncBookmarks: Settings/tabs sync per release notes; bookmarks unverified
featureNotes.agenticBrowsing: Skills and Live Groups; autonomy limited/unverified
featureNotes.aiKillSwitch: Not a documented single switch; AI is central
